title: File Handles
keywords: files, directories, streams, and data storage
learning_outcomes: Explain what file handles contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: fopen().
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: File and stream operations cross a storage boundary. Check operation results, constrain paths, account for permissions and concurrent access, and validate uploads before they become trusted data. In this lesson, focus on fopen(); then compare it with fread(). Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use file handles when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.text: File and stream operations cross a storage boundary. Check operation results, constrain paths, account for permissions and concurrent access, and validate uploads before they become trusted data. For file handles, begin with fopen(). content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for File Handles
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$file = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), "php-course-");
if ($file === false) { throw new RuntimeException("Cannot create temp file"); }
file_put_contents($file, "ready\n");
echo trim((string) file_get_contents($file)) . PHP_EOL;
unlink($file);

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring a failed read or write.
common_mistakes.why: Partial or missing data can be mistaken for successful completion.
common_mistakes.fix: Check return values and throw or report a controlled error when required.

common_mistakes.why: Paths can escape the intended directory.
common_mistakes.fix: Use a controlled storage root and reject paths outside it.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting an uploaded filename or extension.
common_mistakes.why: Names and client-provided content types can be forged.
common_mistakes.fix: Generate storage names, enforce size/type policy, and isolate uploaded files.
